figures.learningGoal: Shows that the City circulates ULA applications only to ATCO Pipelines, so the Designer must contact other pipeline companies directly.
figures.caption: Simplified notification paths. The City ULA administrator circulates applications only to ATCO Pipelines. Other pipeline companies learn of a project only if the Designer applies to them directly for a high pressure pipeline crossing and/or a proximity agreement.
figures.alt: Diagram with four boxes. An arrow runs from Designer to the City ULA administrator, and a second arrow labeled circulates runs from the City to ATCO Pipelines. A crossed-out dashed line labeled not circulated runs from the City to Other pipeline companies. A solid arrow labeled applies directly runs from Designer to Other pipeline companies.

composition.omitted: No further figures. Existing figures already cover the process flow, flowchart lanes, stakeholder responses, permit conditions and the 0.3 m crossing clearance; more would repeat them. Drawing standards, the appendix list, governing codes and EPCOR streetlight support are lists or facts that a picture would not clarify.

fixes: Label the Designer-to-City arrow, for example "applies", so readers know what that path means.
Move "circulates" closer to its arrow. At y=78 it sits about 60px above the line and spans both box tops, which weakens the link between label and path.
Raise label size from 28px to about 32px. At 28px, text drops to about 12.6px on a 360px screen.
Remove the redundant stroke-dasharray='0' on the Other pipeline companies box.
